# The closing-file packet — generated

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build_packet.py from content/closing_packet.json and
     the 50-state table in docs/states/README.md. Do not edit: run the script. -->

**What this is.** The transaction checklist the Academy teaches, as data. It assembles a closing FILE — the documents to demand, the clauses to read, and the unknowns each contingency exists to resolve. It contains no clause language and drafts nothing: every state-sensitive item is written as a QUESTION FOR COUNSEL, never as a statement of what the law is.

**What this is not.** Not a contract, not a form, not legal advice, and not a claim about any state's law. See docs/CONTRACT_ANATOMY.md for the line this platform will not cross, and docs/states/README.md for the record-layer facts that carry sources and dates.

Last reviewed: 2026-09-11. The app renders this same data in the
Underwriting tab, keyed to the edition's state and the property's asset class;
[`src/packet.js`](../src/packet.js) is the renderer.

---

## Clause families — what each piece is FOR, and what to ask counsel

Every row below is state-sensitive, which is why the third column is a question
rather than an answer. This platform does not assert what a state's law says
([`CONTRACT_ANATOMY.md`](CONTRACT_ANATOMY.md)); it gets you to counsel with the
right question already written down.

| Clause family | What it does | Ask counsel | Course |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parties & capacity | Names who binds whom; an entity needs authority documents before it can sign. | What does my entity have to produce in this state to prove authority to sign, and who has to sign it? | E6 |
| Property description | The legal description, not the mailing address. | Which recorded description governs here — plat, metes-and-bounds, or the square/lot form used in Louisiana practice — and does the one in the contract match the recorder's? | V2 |
| Purchase price & deposit | Price, earnest money, who holds it, and when it becomes at-risk. | Who may hold the deposit in this state, under what trust or escrow rules, and what makes it non-refundable? | E5 |
| Financing contingency | The exit if the loan fails: amount, rate ceiling, deadline. | How must notice be given to preserve this exit, and by when? | C3 |
| Inspection / due diligence | The exit for condition, with a defined window and delivery duties. | What access am I entitled to, and what is local practice on re-inspection and repair negotiation? | F6 |
| Disclosures | What the seller must tell the buyer. | Which disclosure forms are mandatory here, what hazard regimes apply (flood, natural hazard, point-of-sale ordinances), and what does this state's caveat-emptor posture put back on me? | F5 |
| Title & survey | Marketable title, exceptions, the title commitment, survey objections. | Is this an attorney state or a title-company state, what survey standard is expected, and which exceptions in the commitment should I refuse? | A3 |
| Closing & possession | Where, when, who conducts it, and when keys change hands. | Who closes in this state — attorney, escrow or title — and which deed form is customary? | M3 |
| Prorations & taxes | Splitting taxes, rents and deposits at closing. | Does the assessment reset on sale here, and am I prorating against the seller's bill or against mine? | N1 |
| Default & remedies | What happens if either side walks: liquidated damages, specific performance. | Which of these remedies is actually enforceable in this state, and what does the foreclosure regime imply if I am the one who fails? | M3 |
| Assignment | Whether the buyer can assign the contract. | Is assignment restricted or licensed in this state, and does what I am planning need a licence? | C4 |
| Tenant provisions | Estoppels, rent-roll delivery, deposit transfer, lease assumption. | What does state and city landlord-tenant law require on deposits and on assuming leases, and is there rent regulation in this municipality? | A4 |

## The document request — by evidence kind

The four kinds are the ones enforced everywhere on this platform
([`INTEROP.md`](INTEROP.md)). A number's kind is where its answer lives, and no
number may migrate to a stronger kind silently.

### public record (7)

| Item | Asset classes | Why | Resolves | Course |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recorded deed / chain of title | all | Establishes what the record says the seller owns. | title | F5 |
| Assessor parcel record and use class | all | The platform's own basis for every value figure; re-pull it yourself. | description | F5 |
| Current tax bill and any delinquency | all | The seller's bill is often not your bill — recompute at your basis. | prorations | N1 |
| Permit history and open code cases | all | Unpermitted work is a title and insurance problem, not a decorating one. | diligence | D3 |
| Zoning verification for the intended use | all | Zoning is local everywhere; the recorded use class is not permission. | description | D2 |
| Certificate of occupancy / legal unit count | multi, apartments, student, lodging, mhp | A unit that is not legal is not income; it is a liability with a tenant in it. | diligence | A2 |
| Environmental and hazard screen for this parcel | all | Flood, subsidence, wildfire and contamination are parcel facts with published layers. | disclosures | F5 |

### document (13)

| Item | Asset classes | Why | Resolves | Course |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current rent roll | multi, apartments, student, mhp | Rents are never public record. The roll you inherit is not the one you underwrote. | tenants | A5 |
| Every lease, in full | multi, apartments, student, mhp, commercial | The document where the money actually lives. | tenants | A4 |
| Signed estoppel certificates | multi, apartments, student, commercial | The tenant's own statement of the deal, which is the one that binds you. | tenants | A4 |
| Security-deposit ledger and transfer | multi, apartments, student, mhp | Deposits are the tenants' money; you assume the obligation at closing. | tenants | A5 |
| T-12 operating statements | multi, apartments, student, lodging, commercial, mhp | Measured history, not hope. Compare line by line against your own expense stack. | diligence | N6 |
| STR / PMS report — ADR, occupancy, RevPAR by month | lodging | Lodging income is a daily business; an annual average hides the season that pays for the year. | diligence | A2 |
| Franchise agreement, PIP and transfer terms | lodging | The brand's required improvement plan is a capital call that arrives with the keys. | diligence | D5 |
| Pad-lease form, utility metering and park rules | mhp | In a pad-rent business the homes and the dirt can have different owners. | tenants | A2 |
| Enrolment and university housing policy for the ring | student | Demand here is a policy decision made by an institution, not a market. | diligence | A7 |
| Preliminary title report / commitment | all | Liens, easements and exceptions — read the exceptions, not the cover. | title | A3 |
| Survey, to the standard local practice expects | all | Where the boundary actually is, versus where the fence is. | title | A3 |
| HOA budget, reserves, litigation and rental caps | condo | A rental cap can make an income thesis illegal on day one. | diligence | A2 |
| Entity formation, good standing and authority to sign | all | The contract binds whoever had capacity to sign it. | parties | E6 |

### quote (2)

| Item | Asset classes | Why | Resolves | Course |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insurance quote in writing | all | The app carries an estimate. An estimate is not a quote and never becomes one by being typed into a quote field. | financing | C2 |
| Lender term sheet or pre-approval matching this structure | all | An offer, not a record. It expires, and the deadline in the contract runs against it. | financing | C3 |

### measurement (2)

| Item | Asset classes | Why | Resolves | Course |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inspection: structure, roof, drainage, sewer lateral, electrical panel | all | The condition unknowns the inspection window exists to resolve. | diligence | D5 |
| Three rent comps from a property manager who leases here | all | The platform's rent basis is index-derived; a manager's comps are the check on it. | diligence | V3 |

## Contingencies — the machinery for resolving unknowns

- **Inspection / due-diligence window** — resolves document and measurement. The window exists to convert condition and operating unknowns into answers before they become losses.
- **Financing contingency** — resolves quote. The exit for the term-sheet unknown. It resolves an offer, not a fact about the world.
- **Title review period** — resolves public record and document. The exit for record unknowns — liens, easements, description mismatches.

> A buyer who signs with unknowns unresolved has converted "unknown" into "assumed" — the exact laundering this platform refuses in its worksheets (docs/INTEROP.md).

## The state layer

Parsed from the 50-state quick reference in [`states/README.md`](states/README.md)
— 51 rows, because that table carries DC alongside the fifty states —
which carries the sources and the review date. Nothing here is restated or added:
if a row there changes, this table changes when the script next runs. Four facts
per state, and the questions above are what you take to a licensed attorney in it.

| State | Guide | Foreclosure | Tax delinquency | Transfer tax | HFA |

| Arkansas | [South Central](states/south-central.md#arkansas) | Both; nonjudicial common | Deed (state land commissioner) | Yes | ADFA |
| California | [Pacific](states/pacific.md#california) | Nonjudicial | Deed | Yes (county documentary) | CalHFA |
| Colorado | [Mountain West](states/mountain-west.md#colorado) | Nonjudicial (public trustee) | Lien | Yes (nominal doc fee) | CHFA |

An edition that spans more than one state resolves to **no state**, and the app
says so rather than picking one — the packet then shows the universal items and
names the state-sensitive ones as unanswerable from this record. Unknown is an
answer.
